We now turn to exploring the non-perturbative sine-Gordon dynamics, by initializing the system at a large global phase displacement ϕ0 (Fig. 5a).

a, We study the dynamics following a large initial phase displacement ϕ0. For ∣ϕ0∣ < π, the plasma-oscillation period is ϕ0-dependent owing to the concavity of U(ϕ). For ϕ0 = π, different regions of the system may eventually settle to different potential minima, which results in domain walls across which ϕ winds by 2π. b, Large-amplitude oscillations. Left: for different ϕ0, the system takes different time, τ, to return to ϕ = 0. Solid lines show sinusoidal fits; for large ϕ0, the oscillation is visibly anharmonic. Each data point is based on five independent experimental runs, and the error bars show the s.e.m. Right: τ/τ0 versus ϕ0; here τ0 = π/(2ωp) is the ϕ0-independent perturbative result. The solid line is the prediction based on the pendulum model. The errors in τ correspond to half of the spacing between the sampled t values. Here, Z0 = 0.31, Ω/(2π) = 74 Hz and μs/(ħΩ) ≈ 11. c,d, Domain walls. The system is prepared at ϕ ≈ π at t = 0, and allowed to relax for 10 ms, corresponding to approximately 7τ0; here Z0 = 0.53, Ω/(2π) = 22 Hz and μs/(ħΩ) ≈ 39. Scale bar, 20 μm. In c, we show examples of domain walls seen in n+ and n− images, where they appear as, respectively, low- and high-density lines; each image shows an independent realization. In d, we show phase maps that reveal the 2π phase winding at domain walls. We interfere the two spin states using a pair of Raman–Bragg laser beams with wavevectors q1,2, and the imaged density distribution, nRB, shows modulations \(\propto \cos ({\bf{q}}\cdot {\bf{r}}+\phi )\), where q = q1 − q2 and r = (x, y). From such fringe patterns we reconstruct the phase maps shown in the bottom panels (see text for details).

Industry observers note that for ∣ϕ0∣ < π, we observe the anharmonic nature of the sine-Gordon potential, \(U(\phi )\propto -\cos (\phi )\), by measuring the time, τ, it takes the system to return from ϕ0 to ϕ = 0 (Fig. 5b). Here, we extract \(\phi =\arctan (Y/X)\), where Y and X are the separately measured projections of the global Bloch vector. In the perturbative regime, U(ϕ) is approximately harmonic and τ ≈ π/(2ωp) is independent of ϕ0. However, as ϕ0 → π, the concavity of U becomes increasingly relevant and τ grows, in analogy with a mechanical pendulum with a large initial angular displacement (solid line in Fig. 5b, right). At longer times these oscillations damp out, and this damping is accompanied by an emergence of spatial structures corresponding to k > 0 excitations (Extended Data Fig. 2).

It has been revealed that for ϕ0 = π, different regions of the system may settle into different potential minima, leading to the formation of domain walls across which ϕ rapidly winds by 2π. We observe such walls in most experimental realizations, with their spatial patterns varying randomly shot to shot (Fig. 5c,d).

In the images of n+ and n− (Fig. 5c), the walls appear as lines of low and high density, respectively. Here we show images from different experimental realizations, but note that if we image both n+ and n− in the same experimental run, we see that they are complementary (Extended Data Fig. 3).

Recent findings suggest that in Fig. 5d, we explicitly demonstrate the 2π phase winding across the domain walls. Here, just before imaging the \(|\uparrow \rangle \) component, we perform a fast (approximately 6 μs) π/2 spin rotation using a resonant two-photon Raman–Bragg coupling (see cartoon) instead of a radio-frequency field. Compared with the radio-frequency field that has a spatially uniform phase across the cloud, the Raman–Bragg coupling leads to a complex Ω with a spatially varying phase q ⋅ r; here r = (x, y) and q = q1 − q2, where q1,2 are the wavevectors of the two laser beams. In the Bloch-sphere picture, the Raman–Bragg Rabi vector always lies in the equatorial plane, but its orientation varies along the direction defined by q. Consequently, the imaged density nRB(x, y) shows modulations \(\propto \cos ({\bf{q}}\cdot {\bf{r}}+\phi )\). For a spatially uniform ϕ, this is a pattern of straight parallel fringes with period 2π/q ≈ 2.51 μm, whereas spatial variations of ϕ(x, y) lead to fringe deformations. In particular, a domain wall perpendicular to q changes the fringe spacing, whereas a wall parallel to q shifts the fringe phase by 2π. In Fig. 5d, we show both  the straight fringes observed at t = 0 ms and two examples of domain walls observed after 10 ms of relaxation; the bottom panels show the reconstructed phase maps (see Extended Data Fig. 4 for more details).

Recent findings suggest that the characteristic width, w, of an equilibrium domain wall is set by the competition between the potential energy per unit length, ∝ ħΩ ⋅ nw, and the corresponding kinetic energy, ∝ ħ2/(2mw2) ⋅ nw. Similarly to the oscillator length in a quantum harmonic oscillator, this competition gives w = ƛ = \({\xi }_{{\rm{M}}}=\sqrt{\hbar /(2m\varOmega )}\).

In a recent development, in Fig. 6a, we extract the domain-wall widths from both the n± images and the phase maps. In all cases, one-dimensional cuts perpendicular to the walls are fitted well by the theoretically predicted10 forms n±(z) = n0 ± n1sech2(z/w) and ϕ(z) = 4arctan[exp(z/w)]; here, z is the coordinate perpendicular to a wall centred at z = 0, and n0, n1 and w are fit parameters. The extracted values of w have a wide distribution (see histograms), probably because our domain walls are excited, but the three mean values are (within one standard deviation) consistent with each other and with the theoretically predicted w, indicated on the histograms by the dashed lines; it is noted that here we include an 8% correction to the predicted w due to our non-zero Z0 (Methods).

Recent findings suggest that a, For the experimental protocol as in Fig. 5, we extract the wall widths, w, from n+ and n− images, such as shown in Fig. 5c, and the phase maps, such as shown in Fig. 5d. We fit cuts perpendicular to the walls to the theoretically expected profiles (solid lines, see text). The histograms show width distributions based on >100 experimental images, and the dashed lines indicate the theoretically predicted w. b, The effect of changing Ω on the domain-wall width. Here the experimental protocol is the same, except that for the last 2 ms of relaxation we jump Ω/(2π) from 22 Hz to either 10 Hz or 45 Hz. The representative n+ images show an increase of the wall widths in the former case and decrease in the latter. Scale bar, 20 μm. The summary of the extracted mean widths is consistent with the expected trend \(w\propto 1/\sqrt{\varOmega }\). The dashed line shows the theoretically predicted w, including an 8% correction due to our non-zero Z0 (Methods). The solid line shows the same trend with systematically 15% lower values. The error bars show the standard deviations of the w distributions. The different symbols corresponding to the same Ω are slightly offset horizontally for clarity.

Industry observers note that finally, in Fig. 6b, we show that the characteristic wall width responds to changes in Ω. Here we initiate the system dynamics as in Fig. 5c, but quench Ω either down or up for the last 2 ms of relaxation. In the representative n+ images, one can see the systematic change in the wall widths, and the widths extracted as in Fig. 6a are consistent with the expected trend \(w\propto 1/\sqrt{\varOmega }\).

To conclude, we have established a versatile analogue simulator for self-interacting relativistic quantum fields with a tunable mass in 2 + 1 dimensions, and observed non-perturbative phenomena that point the way to many future studies. The damping of the global ϕ oscillations, accompanied by an emergence of spatial structures (k > 0 excitations), is expected to be analogous to cosmological preheating and reheating11,12. The π phase jump that places the field at the top of the sine-Gordon potential initiates dynamics associated with a quench through a discrete symmetry-breaking phase transition (with the energy minima changing from ϕ = π to ϕ = 0 and 2π). Generalizing the π phase jump to a ramp of Ω from a positive to a negative value, one can study the associated Kibble–Zurek mechanism50, linked to the formation of topological defects such as cosmic strings and domain walls13,14. Studies of domain-wall networks could provide insights into cosmological dark-matter production in axion scenarios51,52 and gravitational-wave signals in a broad family of particle-physics models53. In this context, a particularly interesting possibility is to use vector light shifts to deterministically imprint specific initial domain-wall configurations and study their subsequent dynamics, including their relaxation and decay54,55. Finally, using Floquet engineering to stabilize the system at ϕ = π would enable studies of false-vacuum decay15,16,41,42 in a relativistic, cosmologically relevant setting17,18,19.

Our experiments were performed in a uniform two-dimensional optical box trap formed by repulsive 532-nm light. The two-dimensional confinement was provided by an accordion lattice with trapping frequency ωz/(2π) ≈ 1 kHz, generated holographically56 with a digital micro-mirror device. The in-plane confinement was provided by a square box directly projected from another digital micro-mirror device through a high-resolution microscope (numerical aperture 0.7). The box size was approximately 50 μm × 50 μm for Fig. 1c, and 30 μm × 30 μm for the rest of the experiments.

The radio-frequency field that couples the two hyperfine states was derived from a vector signal generator (Keysight N5172B). Using in-phase and quadrature modulation, we independently and simultaneously controlled the amplitude, phase and frequency of the radio-frequency field; to prevent carrier feed-through from contaminating the signal, we used a 200-kHz baseband offset. This allowed us to dynamically attenuate the radio-frequency power by >60 dB, and realize Ω/(2π) ≲ 10Hz while retaining the ability to perform fast π/2 rotation at Ω/(2π) > 10kHz. The calibration error for Ω was ≲1% (standard deviation).

Recent findings suggest that to stabilize the magnetic field B, we first regulated the current through our coils using a feedback loop with a bandwidth >1 kHz and then cancelled the residual 50-Hz mains oscillations using feedforward. This cancelled most of the high-frequency noise from the power supply. To counter slow thermal drifts, we periodically (approximately once per minute) calibrated the field using partial Landau–Zener transfers. On the basis of Zerr from the calibration data, we estimated the residual field variations to be about 150 μG (root mean square).

It has been revealed that in the main text we give the simpler and more intuitive approximate equations that assume Z0 = 0. For all expressions in the main text other than equations (2) and (3), for which the exact forms can be obtained from equations (9) and (11), the corrections due to non-zero Z0 can be incorporated by simply replacing Ω by Ω′ and μs by \({\mu }_{{\rm{s}}}^{{\prime} }\). For our experiments, these corrections are usually negligible (compared with the statistical errors), as we illustrate in Fig. 3c by plotting both the predictions that take into account the Z0 corrections (dotted lines) and the approximate predictions that assume Z0 = 0 (solid lines). For Figs. 4 and 5, the corrections are similarly negligible and for simplicity we ignore them, using only the simpler theory given in the main text. The only perceptible correction, which we do include when comparing the data with theory, is in Fig. 6, where, for Z0 = 0.53, the expected wall width \(w=\sqrt{\hbar /(2m{\varOmega }^{{\prime} })}\) is approximately 8% smaller than \(\sqrt{\hbar /(2m\varOmega )}\).

In Extended Data Fig. 1, we also examine the range of k values for which the dispersion of our spin modes, ωs(k) in equation (5), mimics well the relativistic dispersion ωr(k) in equation (6). As long as k < 1/ξs, the difference between ωs and ωr is ≲20% even for Ω = 0, and it reduces with increasing Ω.

Industry observers note that most importantly, the domain walls we observe in Figs. 5 and 6 are deep in the long-wavelength, relativistic regime. For these walls, the relevant k modes are k ≲ 1/w, and even for our largest Ω in Fig. 6, 1/w is still smaller than the smallest 1/ξM (purple dashed line) shown in Extended Data Fig. 1. In this k range, ωs(k) and ωr(k) are essentially identical.

According to recent reports, in Extended Data Fig. 2, we illustrate how the large-amplitude plasma oscillations, such as shown in Fig. 5b, damp at long times. This damping is accompanied by emergence of spatial structures corresponding to a transfer of energy from k = 0 to higher-k modes; qualitatively, this is what is expected in models of cosmological preheating and reheating11,12.

In a recent development, in Extended Data Fig. 3, we create domain walls as in Fig. 5c, and take consecutive images of n+ and n− in the same experimental run, which demonstrates that the two density distributions are complementary.

It has been revealed that from our nRB(x, y) images, we extract ϕtot = q ⋅ r + ϕ using a convolutional neural network59, trained on synthetic data that mimic the experimental images. The network generates quadrature maps I(x, y) and Q(x, y) that approximate, respectively, \(\cos [{\phi }_{{\rm{tot}}}(x,y)]\) and \(\sin [{\phi }_{{\rm{tot}}}(x,y)]\), and we extract ϕtot(x, y) as the phase of I(x, y) + iQ(x, y).

Recent findings suggest that in Extended Data Fig. 4, we illustrate the fidelity of this extraction for two examples shown in Fig. 5d and two additional ones from the same dataset. Left to right, we show: (1) the nRB images, (2) the reconstructed \([1+\cos ({\phi }_{{\rm{tot}}})]/2\), which is essentially the de-noised version of the fringes seen in nRB, (3) the contours tracing the maxima of the reconstructed fringes, (4) the overlaying of these contours on the original images, and (5) the extracted ϕ(x, y).

We obtain ϕ(x, y) from ϕtot(x, y) by subtracting the independently calibrated carrier phase q ⋅ r, but note that, because the relative phase between the Raman–Bragg beams and the radio-frequency coupling is random, our measurement determines ϕ(x, y) only up to a global offset. We fix this offset such that ⟨eiϕ⟩ is real and negative for t = 0 ms (as ϕ is jumped to π), and real and positive for t = 10 ms (appropriate for relaxation to ϕ = 0 (mod 2π), as observed in the n± images).

BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.
  • Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW said.
  • Recent findings suggest that the main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.

Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW said.

Recent findings suggest that the main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China. Although the company sold more cars in the US and Europe compared to the same period last year, this could only partially offset the decline in China.

BMW's car deliveries in China, which were already at their lowest level since 2017 last year, fell 24.8% in the quarter and consequently dragged global deliveries down by 6.3.

CEO Milan Nedeljkovic mentioned his firm would "specifically intensify and accelerate structural measures.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

BMW on Tuesday also lowered its outlook for the current year, citing the faster-than-planned implementation of restructuring measures that includes 8,000 layoffs in its home market.

German carmakers have been struggling to compete with their Chinese counterparts in the electric vehicle market,  resulting in cost-cutting measures.

Volkswagen, the world's second-largest carmaker, is battling mounting competition from falling demand in its core Chinese market.

BMW, and its industry heavyweight peers, Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz, have announced plans to scale back production and reduce costs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Volkswagen Group posted its worst quarterly results in more than a decade earlier this October.

It is looking to cut about 15% of its workforce worldwide, or 100,000 jobs, by the end of the decade. BMW has confirmed that it will cut up to 8,000 jobs — about 5% of its workforce — by the end of 2027.

On the other hand, German auto parts supplier Schaeffler unveiled on Tuesday that it planned to cut almost 3,500 jobs and close five sites in Europe, by 2028.

According to the company statement, three-fourths of the 3,460 job cuts and four of the five site closures will be in Germany.

German automotive supplier Bosch, the world's biggest, confirmed last year that it would cut 13,000 jobs, mostly in its auto division.

#1542. Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner

📅 27 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 25m • 📚 Deep Dive (4970 w)

Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner

📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane mentioned as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or.
  • Industry observers note that in truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre.
  • Sources indicate that kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane mentioned as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Wow indeed. “I am speechless,” Kane added before launching into a heartfelt speech, the wobble in his voice showing just how much this meant to him.

Industry observers note that in truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre. “All those years of sacrifice,” he noted of his parents, Pat and Kim, his voice faltering more than ever at that moment. It was from the heart. And faltering again as he spoke about his wife and “best friend” Katie Goodland. “This is a trophy we all celebrate,” he said, talking to his children back in Bavaria. “I bring a few others [trophies] home but this one is a special one.”.

Sources indicate that kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football. “Lastly for me it is the journey,” he mentioned. “Learn through resilience, determination and self-belief. My journey was not easy and I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration.”.

So much for the “one-season wonder”. So much for the doubters who poured scorn on him. So much for those who believed he would never make it after loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. With varying degrees of success.

Industry observers note that kate Scott, the presenter, perfectly detected the emotion and stated: “You held it together. You got through it.” It showed how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied: “Yes”.

What a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany.

Industry observers note that kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best.

Kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. Those numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world class and legendary.

Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg.

For his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European leagues. And the most since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15. Kane won last season’s Golden Shoe by nine goals from Erling Haaland. He reached his century of Bundesliga goals last month in just 98 games, destroying Dieter Müller’s record set 49 years ago – he took 129 matches.

Kane became one of only two players in history (the other is Ronaldo) to score 20-plus goals across World Cups and European Championships and was the only one to score in two major club cup finals, including a hat-trick. Neither Kylian Mbappé nor Lamine Yamal, his closest rivals, scored in any finals.

Both gave interviews declaring why they should win the Ballon d’Or. Kane? “I don’t like talking about myself,” he stated. “The 73 goals speak for themselves.” They do.

Those are the facts, but there is also the football and, yes, the conduct. Kane has scored some superb goals during that period, not least for England. Take his two goals against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the World Cup that saved his team and Thomas Tuchel from an embarrassing early exit.

The Prince of Wales, who has been FA president since 2006, congratulated Kane on “a fantastic achievement”.

“A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments,” Prince William wrote on Instagram.

It has been revealed that kane, the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the award, is also the ultimate team player – so fulfilling that “collective performance” criteria – and a captain who leads by example on and off the pitch. Fair play? He was last booked in January and was cautioned just three times in 68 games and not at all in any of his 13 appearances this season.

And he works hard, so very hard. Kane was in the top 10 for total distance covered at the World Cup, despite playing a game fewer than most of the others on the list. And he is often seen winning as many defensive headers in his own penalty area as attacking ones in the opposition’s.

Sources indicate that that work extends to off the pitch, to try to maximise his ability, to do everything to be the best version of himself and to be the best. Which he has now been recognised as. And it stems from his winning mentality. Some scoffed when Kane walked into England’s press conference before the 2018 World Cup and remarked he could be top-scorer – but he proved them wrong.

In a recent development, they probably also scoffed at the notion that he would one day be declared the best player in the world and win the Ballon d’Or. But he has done all that. It confirms England’s all-time cap holder (for now jointly with Peter Shilton) and goalscorer as one of the greats. And we are privileged to witness that greatness. Wow, what a night.

By Christian FalkGermany do not have a single player among the 30 in the running to win the Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night – but Bayern Munich do have England captain Harry Kane.

Industry observers note that for the 35-time German champions, the award is perhaps even more important than it is for the peerless striker himself. The Bayern hierarchy are planning to travel to the Palladium Theatre en masse to support Kane.

Kane is not only Bayern’s top striker, he is their international figurehead and, internally, their poster-boy professional. Club patron and honorary president Uli Hoeness described the England captain as the best signing in the club’s history. Hoeness even went so far as to say he loves Kane, and he is not alone in this.

Industry observers note that there's only one Harry Kane. https://t.co/NfZEFmjaUN.

Hoeness is one of many in the club’s leadership who have been endlessly promoting Kane to help the 33-year-old fulfil his lifelong dream of winning the trophy. Bayern officials have been campaigning on his behalf for weeks.

First up was manager Vincent Kompany, who remains in hospital for tests after collapsing at Bayern’s training ground on Friday. Kompany said: “If he can now crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be fitting given the way he plays for the team.”.

The plaudits kept coming. Whether it was sporting director Max Eberl (“He has more than earned the Ballon d’Or. Anyone who loves football loves characters like Harry Kane”), chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen (“One thing is clear – anyone talking about this year’s greatest individual honours cannot overlook Harry Kane”) or president Herbert Hainer (“Harry Kane embodies the idea that sporting greatness is incomplete without greatness of character. He would be a worthy World Footballer of the Year”), everyone at the club is fighting for Kane.

The official Ballon d’Or website has declared Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as winners of the main prize in an embarrassing blunder for the organisation.

Three separate articles were published before rapidly being taken down.

The headline on Kane’s article read: ‘Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season’.

The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

The choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

Recent findings suggest that kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

Last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

In a recent development, in total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

The official ceremony begins at 8pm GMT.

Tech Report: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) stated in a statement on Wednesday that the impact of last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision requiring it to reinstate Russia to international play had been "significantly underestimated.".
  • It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward.".
  • Shortly after Russia rolled out its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the IIHF barred its teams from competing in international ice hockey tournaments, citing security concerns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) stated in a statement on Wednesday that the impact of last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision requiring it to reinstate Russia to international play had been "significantly underestimated.".

It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward.".

Shortly after Russia rolled out its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the IIHF barred its teams from competing in international ice hockey tournaments, citing security concerns. In last Friday's ruling, the CAS said that the IIHF's concerns were "not supported by sufficient evidence.".

Wednesday's statement comes after two days of talks by the IIHF Council aimed at charting a way forward following Friday's CAS decision, which appears to have caught most of the international ice hockey community off guard.

Two of the organizing committees the statement refers to are those of Canada, which is due to host the IIHF World Junior Championship starting next month, and Germany, which is to host the IIHF Men's World Championship next May. Both countries are strong supporters of Ukraine in its war against Russia, and both have expressed serious reservations about their upcoming tournaments in light of the CAS ruling.

On Tuesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney ruled out allowing Russians to compete in the World Juniors in Alberta.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he told reporters at a press conference in Antigua, where he was attending a Commonwealth meeting.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there.".

Last weekend, Frank Lutz, chairman of the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) conceded in a television interview that following the CAS decision, the DEB would "also have to consider the option of handing back (hosting rights to) this championship.".

In a statement to DW on Wednesday, a German government spokesperson reiterated Berlin's position on the matter from the weekend, saying it viewed Friday's CAS ruling "very critically.".

The spokesperson also said  the government would "consult with the German Ice Hockey Federation in the near future regarding the potential consequences of this decision, including its impact on the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany.".

Meanwhile, the ice hockey association of Finland, the defending men's world champions, has been spearheading an effort to boycott upcoming IIHF tournaments should the Russians be allowed to compete.

"We are at the moment working to bring as many countries as possible into a united front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia under these circumstances," Finnish Ice Hockey Association boss Heikki Hietanen said in a statement released on the organization's website on Monday.

"Our stance is that we will not play against Russia as long as the war of aggression against Ukraine continues," added Hietanen, who is also a member of the IIHF Council.

Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Czechia have since made similar statements.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," Swedish Ice Hockey Federation boss Anders Larsson said.

This came shortly after Norway mentioned it would not play Russia at the Men's World Championship and the Danish Ice Hockey Federation issued a similar statement on its website.

Industry observers note that "Denmark will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," it read. Denmark did not qualify for the World Juniors.

Czechia Ice Hockey Association President Alois Hadamczik confirmed on Tuesday that they too would refrain from playing Russian teams.

Latvia's federation noted it “reaffirms its longstanding and firm position" not to play against Russia or its ally Belarus.

Alexander Helwig, chairman of the Austrian Ice Hockey Association told public broadcaster ORF that “as of now, we would certainly not play against Russia.".

USA Hockey has yet to comment on the CAS ruling.

At the same time, sponsors of IIHF tournaments are also getting cold feet. Skoda, which has been the main sponsor of the Men's World Championship for more than three decades, told the Associated Press that it would "reassess" its position if Russia takes part.

"We do not support the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision regarding the participation of Russian national teams in IIHF competitions. With Russia's aggression continuing, we believe the Russian national team's return to the world championship is incompatible with the values we have consistently upheld," the Czech carmaker said.

Skoda isn't alone either, Finnish tire manufacturer Nokian had mentioned it would end its backing if Russia took part and Swedish furniture maker AJ Products, whose logo has been seen on the boards and officials' jerseys at World Championships since 1989, said Monday it would ask for its logo not to be shown.

On Wednesday afternoon, yet another sponsor joined the list, with German workwear tech giant Strauss saying it would "forgo all logo exposure associated with the (men's) tournament" and was considering withdrawing its sponsporship entirely.

With the IIHF Council having failed to agree on how to proceed during its meetings on Monday and Tuesday, President Franz Reindl told Germany's SID news agency on Wednesday, that it would reconvene for further talks on Thursday.

It has been revealed that this article was originally published on November 4, 2026. It was updated on November 5, 2026 with the German government statement to DW.

European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.

It has been revealed that one source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are mentioned to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.

Sources indicate that italy was also a potential destination for Alisson last summer after Juventus held talks with his camp. At one point, Juve fancied their chances of signing him.

Both players will, as it stands, be able to negotiate a free transfer to overseas clubs from January 1, but both Alisson, 34, and Van Dijk, 35, want to stay at Anfield.

It puts the ball in the court of Julian Ward, Liverpool's sporting director, who must decide what to do next.

There had been a long-standing unwritten rule at owners Fenway Sports Group of never extending deals for those over the age of 30, but this was broken in the exceptional cases of Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah 18 months ago, after the pair led Liverpool to their 20th league title.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is keen to stay at the club despite reported interest from his native Brazil.

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk (right) also wants to extend his contract at Liverpool – even though AC Milan are showing interest.

Despite both players wanting to stay on Merseyside, there is understandably a great deal of interest from around the world in taking them on, with local reports linking several Brazilian clubs to Alisson recently.

According to recent reports, van Dijk is a regular at Liverpool youth-team matches, which reveals his love of the club but may also lead to suggestions the Dutchman will move into youth coaching when he does hang up his boots. He took the first-team squad to the Liverpool FC Museum recently to learn more about the club's history – further highlighting his passion for the Reds.

Interest from abroad only strengthens the hands of Alisson and Van Dijk, however, when it comes to their demands over the salary and duration of their upcoming deals.

It has been revealed that alexis Mac Allister is another with an uncertain future, though his father and agent Carlos is hoping to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks. The Argentine's future is less of a pressing issue for the Reds, though, given his deal runs until summer 2028.

Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas are among the other players whose contracts are up in June next year.

Industry observers note that it was around this time last year that the wheels started to fall off the Arne Slot machine. The Dutchman was eventually sacked and we have not heard much from him since. One question I am often asked is what is Slot up to – and why has he fallen off the face of the earth?

Well, I can reveal the former Reds boss is biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones, including several trips to Ibiza. Slot and his son Joep have also visited South America, taking in games in Argentina and Brazil.

Sources indicate that slot, who has also been attending matches at home, turned down the Netherlands national team job and a lucrative gig in Saudi Arabia. He also rejected approaches in the summer from clubs including AC Milan, who eventually plumped for former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.

He is waiting for the right opportunity and does not believe his stock has fallen in the same way, for example, as several axed United or Chelsea bosses. After all, Slot won the Premier League title and would be a fine hire for most clubs around Europe.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (centre, bottom row) watches the Dutch Eredivisie match between Heerenveen and his old club Feyenoord earlier this month.

Slot is waiting for the right job to come up – emboldened by the knowledge he is a Premier League winner.

…but AI report makes grim reading for Arne.

Reds hunt for academy recruitment guru.

Liverpool are in the process of hiring an academy ‘talent ID lead’ to help with their youth recruitment.

Sources indicate that regular readers of this column will know this area is a key metric Anfield chiefs measure success by. They are now hiring someone responsible for leading the identification and recruitment of academy talent between the ages of 13 and 18 across the UK and Ireland.

Notable recent arrivals from other academies at this age include current first-teamers Rio Ngumoha, Conor Bradley, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell.

Kop Kids: Amazing Abe lights up England duty.

Confidential readers will recall I revealed on October 15 that Joshua Abe was ahead of schedule in his recovery from a shoulder injury and set for just another month on the sidelines. And Abe was indeed on the pitch representing England Under 17s exactly a month later, scoring against Montenegro and then again against Poland on Saturday.

Industry observers note that in the last 12 months, the 16-year-old has 14 goals and four assists in just over 1,200 minutes played. Those are phenomenal numbers and it would not be a surprise to see the winger back in the first-team training group again soon.

Joshua Abe has recovered from a shoulder injury and was back in action for England Under 17s this week.

Fancy running the line, Andoni?

Recent findings suggest that in the last break, the boss was spotted at the women’s Merseyside Derby. Now, he has been pictured at a local Sunday League match, taking pictures with youngsters who could not believe their luck.

These may seem like small gestures but they are a helpful way of winning hearts and minds among a fanbase whose pleas for Slot to take an active interest in all aspects of the club sometimes fell on deaf ears.

Manchester United are in town on Sunday, in case you needed reminding.

Since winning the Premier League title last year, Liverpool’s league record against the 'Substantial Six' is played 12, won two, drawn three, lost seven. That must improve, starting on Sunday, and there can be no excuses around a newly introduced-manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino - who will barely have had time to find his parking space at Carrington by the time he comes to Anfield.

Sources indicate that liverpool need to see more from their significant-money signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who have been excellent for most of the season but poor in some high-profile fixtures, such as the home defeats by Manchester City and Arsenal. Across his 19 games against Liverpool, Pochettino has only won three matches, drawing five and losing 11.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards. The occasion was the world premiere of "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" (released in the US and India as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone").

"Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.

In a recent development, daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle. The BBC quoted him as saying, "It is so cool. I have never heard my name shouted so much in an hour.".

The crowds revealed just how far Harry Potter fever had spread in only four years.

The first Harry Potter book was published by Britain's Bloomsbury in June 1997, with an initial print run of just 500 hardcover copies.

About 5,000 paperback copies were also released around the same time.

Recent findings suggest that today, first editions are prized collectors' items, with hardcover copies commanding high prices at auction. In mid-October, one sold for $400,000 through US auction house Heritage Auctions.

Industry observers note that at first, the book's popularity grew largely by word of mouth among schoolchildren. Media attention followed when it won the prestigious Nestle Smarties Book Prize later that year.

With an estimated 120 million-plus copies sold worldwide, it is the best-selling book in the series and ranks among the best-selling novels of all time.

Industry observers note that for years, J.K. Rowling's public image was defined by her extraordinary rise from a single mother on welfare to a billionaire.

But in recent years, debate over her views on gender and transgender identity has increasingly overshadowed that success. It's an issue Rowling herself frequently weighs in on.

According to recent reports, in an essay published on her website on October 21, 2026, Rowling reiterated her opposition to what she calls the "current, dominant strain of trans activism." She argues that this movement "holds that a man who declares himself a woman is, literally, a woman, and is therefore entitled to be treated as a woman in all contexts." Rowling argues that allowing trans women into single-sex spaces poses a risk. She describes biological sex as an indisputable biological fact.

Such statements have led critics to accuse Rowling of transphobia, while others regard her stance as a defense of women's rights and safety.

According to recent reports, the controversy has also divided her fans. Some stand by Rowling, while others try to draw a distinction between the books and their author.

Others have left Harry Potter behind altogether. One former fan is German YouTuber Coldmirror, known for her Harry Potter parodies. The media artist from the Bremen area, whose real name is Kathrin Fricke, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper: "I don't have any love left for Harry. I'm still somewhat interested, but I can no longer watch it in good conscience." She cited Rowling's campaigning against transgender people as the reason.

Sources indicate that the "Harry Potter" film cast is divided as well. The three main stars — Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint — have publicly spoken out in support of transgender people. Meanwhile, Ralph Fiennes, who played Lord Voldemort, and Helena Bonham Carter, who portrayed Bellatrix Lestrange, have defended Rowling's right to express her views.

Recent findings suggest that despite the controversy surrounding Rowling, Warner Bros., which holds the Harry Potter film rights, is bringing the books back to the screen — this time as a series for HBO. The premiere is scheduled for December 25.

The eight-episode first season is an an adaption of the first book. Even though the episode lengths haven't been confirmed, the scope of a TV series gives each book much more room than the original films did. That means more time to explore subplots, character development and everyday life at Hogwarts. While many fans are looking forward to a more detailed adaptation, others remain skeptical. They find it hard to imagine the familiar characters being played by anyone else.

The new trio consists of Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley.

J.K. Rowling is an executive producer on the show. HBO claims, however, that her views on gender identity won't be reflected in the storyline. Several people involved in the new production have publicly distanced themselves from her views. Paapa Essiedu, who has been cast as Severus Snape, signed an open letter supporting transgender people. Rowling subsequently noted she had neither the power nor the desire to have him removed from the show because of it. John Lithgow, who plays Dumbledore, and Nick Frost, who portrays Hagrid, have also spoken out against Rowling's views.

Meanwhile, the Harry Potter merchandising machine is still going strong. On November 4, Britain's largest Harry Potter store to date is set to open in London. According to Warner Bros., the two-story shop covers more than 1,950 square meters.

#1534. Tech Report: Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1696 w)

Tech Report: Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1696 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement’s temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

According to recent reports, the man parked up in a nondescript green Ford Fiesta cut an incongruous sight in the affluent residential neighbourhood of Casal Palocco, in south-west Rome, but no one paid him much notice. He made no eye contact and at no stage stepped from the car.

It was only after the street’s famous resident, AS Roma’s Belgian midfielder Radja Nainggolan, had his home burgled and an extraordinary £400,000 worth of possessions stolen that the player’s then wife, Claudia, six months pregnant at that time in April 2016, recalled the Eastern European-looking man in the battered vehicle up their street.

He was Vlada Djuric, a 50-year-old Macedonian of Romani descent and part of the wider Nikolov family, including his wife Zora Jovanovic, their two sons and daughter, whose highly organised thefts from the homes of top footballers would continue for more than a decade, with imprisonment deemed only a minor setback.

While the Nainggolans were blithely unaware of the criminal family’s lookout man – they’d gone to visit friends nearby for a couple of hours and hadn't even bothered to activate the burglar alarm – the assailants were primed to seize the chance.

The two sons, Valentino and Giacomo, mounted the villa’s perimeter wall, opening one door with a magnetic card and jimmying another with a screwdriver, and proceeded undisturbed through the house in 27 minutes, throwing the proceeds of their burglary into a bag as they went.

There were 15 watches (Rolex, Patek Philippe and others) valued at £250,000 and 20 pieces of jewellery, including a diamond worth £25,000. Security cameras on a landing and in an internal room filmed them but such was their confidence, they only partially covered their faces.

Former Roma midfielder Radja Nainggolan and his then wife Claudia, who was six months pregnant, were the targets of a burglary in 2016 (Source: Instagram/Claudia_lai_82).

Nainggolan had an extraordinary £400,000 worth of possessions taken, including 15 watches.

It was old-fashioned detective work from a local officer, Bruno Failla, which led police to a rambling home at Lurano, a small town six hours drive away in Lombardy, at which the Nikolovs would lavishly entertain other members of the Romani community.

The watches matched the descriptions of those stolen from the Nainggolans, though it was a necklace with a Roma logo, and the pair of red shoes with Nainggolan's initials, which really gave the game away.

In a recent development, ‘I ask again for vigilance and watchfulness, please,’ Failla said at the time, because this was the fourth time that footballers' properties in Casal Palocco had been targeted in the space of five years. But the challenge of placing footballers in a state of constant vigilance became clear fully seven years on, when another Nainggolan residence, in Antwerp, Belgium, was burgled while his relatives held a party there.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It is one of the most complicated and consistently challenging parts of our security work,’ one former special forces soldier now providing security for footballers tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘It’s been a substantial sector of our work for years now, but the movements of these clients are so public and that’s irresistible to criminals. The wealth is very evident.’.

One of the sons, Valentino, was jailed for two years in 2016 and other members of his family also did time, but once out, they all set their sights on the Premier League. In 2024, they arrived in the UK via a ferry to Dover from Calais, stopped off in London and made their way north, sleeping in a Ford motorhome and travelling to target homes in a Citroen C3.

A spree of attacks ensued from them on the homes of Alexander Isak, then a Newcastle player, Wolves’ Matheus Cunha (who has subsequently been burgled again while at Manchester United), Birmingham City’s Neil Etheridge and Leon Bailey, with Aston Villa at the time.

A number of Premier League clubs, including Liverpool, Everton and United, are known to have appointed their own security teams to provide an around-the-clock presence at the homes of players who are in squads playing away from home – rather than have that in the hands of a range of private operators.

The house burglars’ modus operandi pales by comparison with some of violence displayed by others who prey on the footballer set. Paul Hughes, managing director of Benchmark Security Group, a leading Manchester-based protection firm, employs former police and Royal security drivers to train his clients in the art of 'defensive driving'.

Techniques include never taking up a position in the middle lane, avoiding the outside lane if there is a central barrier, and always maintaining sight of the tyres of the vehicle in front when you slow.

'If you can see the tyres, you will always have room to manoeuvre right or left of the car in front, at speed, without hitting it,' Hughes notes.

Sportswear giants adidas have linked up with Manchester-born streetwear brand Drama Call to deliver a nostalgic Manchester United collection inspired by the clubâs 1991 Cup Winnersâ Cup triumph.

The centrepiece of the drop is a reimagined version of the â91 final shirt â a design forever etched into United history.

This updated take arrives in a long-sleeved white base with red Three Stripes, the adidas Trefoil, and the club crest, while Drama Call apply their own twist through a stylised star logo. It features on the sleeve in place of a competition badge, on the collars and cuffs, and as a faint oversized motif across the front.

In a recent development, beyond the shirt, the collection expands into lifestyle territory. Half-zip tracksuits, hoodies, tees, caps and even a football all carry the same mix of adidas heritage, United identity and Drama Callâs bold graphics.

The fusion of club tradition with streetwear sensibility creates a capsule that feels equally at home on the terraces and the high street.

United players themselves highlighted off the new gear as they arrived at Old Trafford before their 3-2 win over Burnley, giving the collection its first public run-out.

And while it was Mark Hughes who proved the hero in the 1991 final against Barcelona with both goals in a 2-1 victory, it was Bruno Fernandes who stepped up against Burnley â tucking away an injury-time penalty to secure another dramatic United win.

Whether in Europe more than three decades ago or in the Premier League today, the shirt seems to carry a touch of luck. Maybe United ought to start wearing it more often.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La Gazzetta dello Sport reports that John Stones’ fitness issues have sparked Inter’s interest in Lazio defender Oliver Provstgaard for next summer.

Inter have set their sights on 23-year-old Lazio defender Provstgaard, according to Gazzetta.

The report claims the defending Serie A champions are already planning to add a new centre-back for next season, also due to Stones’ physical problems.

Lazio’s asking price for the Denmark international is close to €40m, a fee the Nerazzurri will only be able to afford at the end of the season, not in the January window.

According to Gazzetta, Davide Frattesi’s move to Lazio over the summer might even help the Nerazzurri to lower Lazio’s demands.

Frattesi joined Lazio in a €5m loan deal last summer, and the Biancocelesti hold an option to buy for a further €10m.

Inter have a 50% sell-on clause, and re-discussing the terms of the agreement might help them get a better deal for Provstgaard in the summer.

Inter saw Stefan de Vrij, Matteo Darmian and Francesco Acerbi leave the club at the end of their contracts in June 2026, replacing them by signing Stones as a free agent from Manchester City and retaining Benjamin Pavard after his return from a one-season loan spell at Marseille.

Stones has struggled with injuries this season and has just returned to training after nearly two months out. The England international suffered a muscle strain in the flexor muscles of his left thigh in mid-September and was an unused substitute in Inter’s latest Serie A match against Como, just before the break.

The England international has made four appearances across all competitions this season, and his contract at the Stadio Meazza expires in June 2028.

Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted.

Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.

Eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent. It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed.

Having chiselled out a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes in which Max Dowman was sent off, Fleetwood dispatched five nerveless spot-kicks, the last one thundered in by Conor Haughey after Bruno Guimarães’s penalty was saved by Jay Lynch.

In a recent development, “You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.”.

This was ignominious for Arsenal, an elimination from this tournament to rival the 1969 loss in the final to Swindon Town or the 2012 exit to Bradford, then also of League Two. What made this so astonishing was the fact that Mikel Arteta went so strong.

You should never be surprised by anything these days, but, even still, an eight-minute delay because of a drone flying over this wonderful little venue would not have been on anyone’s bingo card. Only 57 seconds had been played when Michael Salisbury, the referee, saw a light in the sky and stated “stop”.

Sources indicate that the anticipation was that Arsenal would saunter clear against opponents who had lost at Exeter City on Saturday, leaving them 18th in England’s fourth tier. But it only took a few skirmishes to appreciate this was not going to be the cakewalk anticipated in what was the biggest occasion in Fleetwood’s history.

Arteta absolutely knew his team were not operating at the levels they should have been. He was wrapped up against the elements in a thick black jacket but, every so often, he would express his exasperation at Jurriën Timber, captain for the night, to “get forward!”.

They were in a battle, that much was obvious, and one challenge from Shaun Rooney – so forceful you thought the ball might burst – sent Myles Lewis-Skelly spinning like a top. How Fleetwood’s fans loved it, roaring their approval as the young England international hit the ground with a thump.

Arsenal had one good chance when Dowman skipped down the right and dragged a shot across the box that Viktor Gyökeres could not divert but then, wonderfully, things took a totally unexpected turn when Fleetwood poked their noses in front.

Sources indicate that it was a League Two goal in its simplicity, but that is no criticism. Harrison Neal helped a long ball forward, putting it behind Marli Salmon and Aaron Loupalo-Bi relished the chance to get into a foot race, grappling with the England Under-17 international.

According to recent reports, salmon looked like he had him at one point, but Loupalo-Bi was strong – not to mention composed – and he held off the challenge to slide a left-footed shot through the legs of Illan Meslier, who was making his Arsenal debut. What followed was unique to the magic of an English cup tie.

They were playing in English football’s sixth tier in 2009, and so while their stadium may share its name with Arsenal’s former home, the two clubs are worlds apart.

The League Cup is fourth of four competitions on Arsenal’s list of priorities, but Mikel Arteta should be able to rotate extensively while progressing to the quarter-finals. With a trip to Anfield on Sunday, that is a welcome luxury.

Kepa Arrizabalaga, Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres are seasoned internationals in need of minutes and in line to start.

According to recent reports, max Dowman lit up Arsenal’s third-round victory at Ipswich Town, and 17-year-old centre-back Marli Salmon was not far behind him. Young striker and Northern Ireland international Ceadach O’Neill is also expected to be involved, and he may be joined by other academy players.

While attention is fixed on Premier League and Champions League success, Arsenal’s stinging defeat by Manchester City in last season’s final of this competition will not have been forgotten by Arteta or his players.

In a recent development, matt Lawlor, Fleetwood’s manager, was full of praise for Arsenal in his pre-match press conference: “The champions are coming to town and they’re coming to our patch. The players need to be excited by it, not overawed by it. The respect is through the roof, but the fear can’t be through the roof.

In a recent development, “We’ve earned a game like this. We’ve had to go through round upon round of tough games, and none of them were easy. To get to where we are, we deserve that.”.

Arteta has told his players that they must keep their standards high, with a lack of concentration or professionalism potentially their worst enemy against fourth-tier opposition.

Industry observers note that arteta said: “Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play. So every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve that, and then try to win and try to play a bit better than them.“We know the risk, and in football, things can get very equal the moment you are able to match certain things, and that’s why our basics and habits have to be through the roof to be able to win the game.”Full team news on the way shortly.

Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat mentioned.
  • In a recent development, themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a major win.
  • "It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat mentioned. "Making history once is something, but making it twice is really something else. I felt very happy and I felt a big relief. Only I know how many sacrifices I made and how many hardships I needed to overcome.".

In a recent development, themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a major win. In Mariam Bsharat's case, it's about more than just dedication to training and taking care of the body. The 17-year-old won her second under-21 World Karate Championship gold medal competing for the Palestine national team in Poland in October.

"It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.

"I faced challenges in transportation," Bsharat said. "I wasn't able to go from one city to another to be able to train with other people, so that I can actually prepare for competitions. I needed to travel to other countries like Jordan or Egypt ... which was very hard for me. And, financially, the support wasn't really the support an elite athlete needed.".

In a recent development, growing up in Nablus, Bsharat had a narrow path to the top. But initially, it was her own reluctance that threatened to stop a champion career before it started.

"When I was a little kid, I did not really love it," noted Bsharat, who competes in the division for fighters who weigh under 66 kilograms (145 pounds).

"I started it because my family was in that sport," Bsharat said. "My father had a dojo, and my mother also did that sport. My siblings and my aunts and my uncles — it's a family thing. I started it because they were all doing it. In time, I started getting into it.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, family has been a constant source of comfort and inspiration for Bsharat. Her father and uncle have acted as manager and coach respectively. While her mother and siblings moved with Mariam to Hamburg, Germany, last year, her father remained in order to take care of his business, the dojo, though he visits and tries to be with his daughter in competitions. Integration has been made easier by her mastery of the language, taught to her by her German mother.

Bsharat has mixed feelings about leaving her homeland.

"I'm thankful to be here because being in Germany opened lot of doors for me, and I think I have a brighter future here," Bsharat noted. "But also being in Palestine was just my everyday life, and I loved it there. My family was around me, my friends were around me, and I just felt comfortable, which was a massive change coming here to Germany. I think every change comes with hardships.".

According to recent reports, as well as the obvious difficulties of living in an area occupied by Israel, there are particular challenges for sportspeople living in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with access to facilities, travel and constant security fears among them. As such, very few people from the Palestinian territories become successful on the international sporting stage. That, Bsharat said, gives her responsibilities that are unusual and heavy for a person of any age, let alone a 17-year-old.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"Being an elite athlete in Palestine is something very special because not everybody in Palestine has that opportunity. There aren't really a lot of athletes that are elite and who win international medals,” Bsharat said.

Sources indicate that "So all that pressure from all the country and all the people, the family, the coaches are on me because I'm representing them, raising their flag,” she said. "I sometimes even forget to fight for myself and actually think about myself.".

That has not yet proved a barrier to Bsharat, who is is ranked first in the world in her category by the World Karate Federation (WKF). With Palestine recognized by the International Olympic Committee, Bsharat would likely have been a contender to raise that flag in Los Angeles at the 2028 Olympics. But the sport was dropped from the Games in 2024.

In a recent development, "The global karate community remains steadfast in our belief that the natural place for karate is within the Olympic Games, and we sincerely hope that the incongruence we suffered in Paris 2024 and LA 2028 will be corrected for Brisbane 2032, if not sooner," the WKF wrote in response to the decision in 2024. The sport was also taken off the slate for the recent Youth Games in Senegal.

Recent findings suggest that should karate return in Brisbane, Bsharat would likely be approaching her prime. In the meantime, she is looking forward to starting her journey as a senior when she turns 18. But she won't be hanging around.

"My goal is it to be a world champion at seniors, which is the hardest and the best thing you can achieve in karate," she mentioned.

"But winning an Olympic medal, being called Olympic champion or just representing my country with that flag [is a thought that] is just full of happiness and pride.".

The interview was conducted by Janek Speight.

Former Juventus midfielder and coach Conte has strongly confirmed his desire to return to the Allianz Stadium one day, predicting that “sooner or later the circle will close.”.

Conte already coached Juventus from 2011 to 2014, winning the first three Serie A titles in the post-Calciopoli era. This is not the first time the Italian tactician has openly admitted his desire to return to the club one day, but that doesn’t mean it will happen.

Recent findings suggest that tuttosport insists Juventus are not considering replacing their coach, Spalletti, this season. First, the Serie A giants still trust the Tuscan tactician; second, they are reluctant to make another managerial change that would bring in their fourth coach in four years.

Club owners and directors are convinced that even appointing Conte midseason would not address the team’s lack of personality or the players’ lack of responsibility, especially with frequent changes on the bench in the coming years.

Spalletti remains under contract until 2028, and the club will assess his results at the end of the season.

If, however, the Bianconeri change coach in 2027-28, Conte might not be their top candidate, Tuttosport claims.

Industry observers note that carnevali, in fact, seems to favour a different option, such as ex-Inter coach Simone Inzaghi. The Piacenza-born tactician might not be every Juventus fan’s cup of tea because of his past with the Nerazzurri, but even Conte’s potential appointment isn’t widely approved, given how he left the club one day into the 2014-15 pre-season and his move to Inter a few years later.

Latest Update: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3405 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6—arising from collective quantum interference among emitters—has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open fresh opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8,9,10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.
